tour_morning_summary: The buyer, sales, the CEO and finance start their day — each sees only what needs them.
tour_morning_1_title: Every role has its own day
tour_morning_1_body: This is Karim Youssef, supply chain. Golden Sea's dashboard is built for the person signed in: his waiting states, his queue, his follow-ups.
tour_morning_2_body: Every live case has an owner, a deadline and a next action. Blocked and at-risk cases come first, then the nearest deadline.
tour_morning_3_body: What changed overnight and what needs him today: deadlines, a PO mismatch, a supplier that hasn't replied, failed integrations.
tour_morning_4_title: Sales sees the same cases — without costs
tour_morning_4_body: Soaad Amer signs in. Her queue has no values, costs or margins: sales never sees what Golden Sea pays its suppliers.
tour_morning_5_body: Karim Balbaa sees what waits for him first — a margin exception from Soaad, a supplier deposit, an FX rate, and a bank change that already has one of its two approvals.
tour_morning_6_body: Mohamed Helmy only sees payments and deposits. He already approved the bank change after a call-back; it now waits for the CEO — two people, always.
tour_morning_7_body: Notifications, bookmarks and the counters in this panel belong to the person signed in. Back as Karim Youssef — his are about his cases.
tour_rfq_to_case_title: Any format in, one case out
tour_rfq_to_case_summary: An RFQ email with Excel, PDF and a photo becomes one clean case — AI reads, a person decides.
tour_rfq_to_case_1_body: Outlook, Gmail, the website quick-quote form and WhatsApp all land in one list — nothing lives in someone's personal mailbox.
tour_rfq_to_case_2_body: A new RFQ for MV Aurora Crest arrives with an Excel list, a PDF and a WhatsApp photo. The email and every file stay with the case.
tour_rfq_to_case_3_body: Every line gets its IMPA code, quantity, unit and the file it came from, with a confidence. The 62% photo line is flagged for a person.
tour_rfq_to_case_4_body: Missing details become a drafted clarification to the customer — drafted, not sent.
tour_rfq_to_case_5_body: Assignment rules suggest who owns it and who backs them up; the deadline comes from the customer's request.
tour_rfq_to_case_6_body: Confirming creates the case with its lines, links the email and sends one branded acknowledgement.
tour_replies_title: Every reply matched, every price remembered
tour_replies_summary: Supplier RFQs go out without the client's name; replies are matched even with new subjects.
tour_replies_1_body: Lines are split by category and each supplier sees only its lines — never the customer or the vessel.
tour_replies_1_target: Each supplier sees only the lines they can quote
tour_replies_2_body: Replies arrive with changed subjects; each is matched to its RFQ by its reference, and reminders stop for that supplier.
tour_replies_3_body: A supplier Golden Sea never bought from replied. It's created automatically, with its price, date and validity.
tour_replies_4_body: An unclear price unit isn't used until someone confirms it.
tour_replies_5_body: The same engine reads the old inboxes into customers, vessels, suppliers and dated prices. Nothing is saved until Karim Balbaa approves.
tour_quote_title: From offers to an approved quotation
tour_quote_summary: The buyer compares and prices, the CEO approves, the customer gets Golden Sea's own layout.
tour_quote_1_title: Cheapest isn't always cheapest on board
tour_quote_1_body: Every offer is normalised to EGP per base unit. Switch to landed cost and freight to Port Said re-ranks them.
tour_quote_2_body: 242 was offered for an exact-part 243 line, so the line is blocked from pricing. v1 is kept for the record; the corrected v2 is used.
tour_quote_3_body: Alexandria stock is cheapest per unit but dearest delivered. The proposal splits 10 + 5 across two suppliers, both before the vessel's ETA.
tour_quote_4_body: Shared charges are spread over the lines; policy is checked on margin, and every line shows cost, charges and profit.
tour_quote_5_body: The quotation and its exceptions go to Karim Balbaa with one click. AI never prices on its own.
tour_quote_6_body: Karim Balbaa sees what he's deciding and why — the margin, the FX rate, the deposit, and the bank change Mohamed Helmy already approved.
tour_quote_7_body: The same quotation in Golden Sea's own layout, in English or Arabic, in EGP or USD. Nothing goes to the customer until a person confirms the email.
tour_po_check_title: The PO doesn't match the quote
tour_po_check_summary: A customer PO with an old price and the wrong quantity is caught before anything is ordered.
tour_po_check_1_title: The PO is checked line by line
tour_po_check_1_body: Nordvik's PO is matched to the approved quotation version. An old pack size, an expired v1 price and 15 instead of 10 helmets block the commitment until the customer agrees in writing.
tour_po_check_2_body: Lines the customer didn't order stay open for a revision or close with a recorded reason.
tour_po_check_3_body: Once the PO is agreed, supplier POs are prepared — drop-shipped or through the warehouse — and each is re-checked against the latest offer first.
tour_po_check_4_body: Each supplier bill is matched to its PO and the goods received; a duplicate bill is refused.
tour_po_check_5_body: Signed in as the CEO: a flagged price change on a supplier PO is shown before he commits, and deposits wait for a payment approval.
tour_delivery_to_cash_title: From the quay to the bank
tour_delivery_to_cash_summary: An ETA change re-plans the delivery, proof of delivery unlocks the invoice, finance collects and pays.
tour_delivery_to_cash_1_title: The vessel moves, the plan follows
tour_delivery_to_cash_1_body: Port, ETA, agent, truck, boarding staff and launch in one plan. When the agent moves the ETA, drop 2 is re-planned and the owner is alerted.
tour_delivery_to_cash_2_body: Two drops for one order. A drop counts as delivered only with the signed delivery note from the vessel.
tour_delivery_to_cash_3_title: Invoice what was delivered, then e-invoice
tour_delivery_to_cash_3_body: Only delivered quantities are invoiced, each invoice goes to the Egyptian tax authority, and rejections or outages get a safe retry.
tour_delivery_to_cash_4_body: Receivables and payables side by side. Supplier payments wait for the Financial Director or the CEO.
tour_delivery_to_cash_5_body: A supplier's new bank account needs a call-back on the number on file and two approvers — Finance and the CEO.
tour_handover_summary: One case from first email to last payment, and a handover AI drafts for a person to confirm.
tour_handover_1_body: From the first email to the last payment, everything happens on one case. GS-RFQ-0142 is comparing offers.
tour_handover_2_body: Three of six lines are ready and one is blocked by a clarification — a case only looks done when every line is.
tour_handover_3_body: Reassigning asks AI for a handover note — open questions, tasks, the customer's contact rule. A person edits and confirms it.
tour_handover_4_body: Automatic steps name the rule that fired; human steps name the person. That's the audit trail.
tour_exceptions_summary: A failed mailbox and a low-confidence AI result, handled safely; urgent RFQs reach the on-duty person.
tour_exceptions_1_body: An expired Outlook token and an unreachable e-invoice signing service sit in a queue with an owner — not in a log nobody reads.
tour_exceptions_2_title: Low confidence waits for a person
tour_exceptions_2_body: Uncertain AI results are never applied automatically; someone reviews them here.
tour_exceptions_3_body: Trigger, owner, due time, approval, retry behaviour and stop condition for each rule — switched on and off by management, and logged.
tour_exceptions_4_body: Outside Sunday–Thursday office hours, urgent RFQs go to the on-duty person, with a backup if nobody answers.
tour_close_summary: Estimates become actuals, FX and claims are accounted for, and only green checks close the case.
tour_close_1_body: The profit promised at quotation against the real result: the launch cost more than estimated once it was billed.
tour_close_2_body: USD 10,000 arrived at 48.80 against the quoted 48.60 — a gain of EGP 2,000, on the case where it happened.
tour_close_3_body: Two helmets cracked in transit; the supplier's credit note settles the claim.
tour_close_4_body: Bills matched, deliveries signed, invoices accepted by the tax authority and paid, claims settled — then the case can close.
tour_control_room_summary: The CEO's control room and Ask Golden Sea — and what Sales is never told.
tour_control_room_1_body: Written at 07:00 from live records, with links to its sources.
tour_control_room_2_body: Questions are answered from the live data, and every answer cites the records it used.
tour_control_room_3_body: Margin by store against the 15% minimum, plus pipeline, speed, cash and supplier performance.
tour_control_room_4_body: Signed in as Soaad Amer, the same assistant declines questions about costs and margins.
tour_growth_summary: Prospects, fleets and vendor registrations — with what to say on the next call.
tour_growth_1_body: Ship managers from first introduction to active account; stalled prospects are flagged.
tour_growth_2_body: Each next step has a short script. Recording the outcome plans the next one.
tour_growth_3_body: Documents and committee dates for getting onto each ship manager's approved-vendor list.
